simple.meaning: נָקַר (nâqar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to bore ( penetrate , quarry ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Numbers, Judges, 1 Samuel, Job, Proverbs, and 1 more, beginning at Numbers 16:14. Its contexts include family, family line, righteousness, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָקַר (H5365).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָקַר (nâqar) / H5365 is traced through Numbers 16:14, Judges 16:21, 1 Samuel 11:2, Job 30:17 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: dig, pick out, pierce, put (thrust) out.
definitions.full: H5365. naqar [ נָקַר ] verb bore, pick, dig (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic נְקַר id. ; Arabic perforate, bore out, hollow out Lane 2838 ; Ethiopic be one-eyed Di 645 ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine plural suffix יִקְּרוּהָ Prov 30:17 ; Infinitive נְקוֺר 1Sam 11:3 , both of boring , or picking out eye (accusative). Pi`el Imperfect . 2 masculine singular תְּנַקֵּר Num 16:14 (JE), 3 masculine plural וַיְנַקְּרוּ Judg 16:21 both of boring out eyes (accusative); Perfect 3masculine singular נִקַּר Job 30:17 he (or it , i.e. the night) boreth my bones מֵעָלָ֑י (of effects of elephantiasis; Bu reads נֻקַּר ). Pu`al Perfect 2masculine plural נֻקַּרְתֶּם Isa 51:1 the quarry (from which) ye were digged .
